assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Eicher Motors (consolidated, Rs crore). Consolidated revenue and EBITDA are Royal Enfield only (motorcycles, spares, accessories, apparel, services; India plus the international subsidiaries). VE Commercial Vehicles (VECV, Eicher 54.4%, joint control with Volvo) is a joint venture accounted for by the equity method: none of its revenue or EBITDA is consolidated and Eicher books 54.4% of VECV's profit as one line ('share of profit of joint venture'), which Screener adds to other income. So the model is: RE volume x revenue per motorcycle (engine volume path; the domestic / international / allied build is in `build` and is checked against model revenue in tools/authoring/EICHERMOT.ctx.js) and VECV volume x realisation -> EBITDA -> PAT -> 54.4% share (block `vecv`), which enters `otherIncome`. Volumes are on the company's financial-statement basis (FY26 1,227,977 = domestic 1,107,343 + international 120,634), which differs slightly from the monthly sales releases (FY26 1,238,659) because CKD exports are counted differently. Screener's Net Profit equals Profit for EPS (no minorities), so no patchRaw. Valued on a sum of the parts (RE P/E + VECV P/E) as the street does; the engine carries the SOTP as an implied P/E on consolidated Sep-28E EPS (tools/authoring/EICHERMOT.sotp.js writes it).

volume._why: Royal Enfield motorcycles, financial-statement basis (FY26 1,227,977, +22.4%). FY27E +15.8% to 1.422 mn: Q1FY27 332,940 (+27.4%; domestic 301,174 +32%, international 31,766 -2%); monthly releases show Jul +34% and Aug +11% (Apr-Aug 575,138, +23%; domestic +28%, exports -9%). We assume domestic +12% for Sep-Mar against the GST-boosted base of FY26 (domestic Sep-Mar FY26 ~699k) -> domestic FY27E 1.304 mn (+17.8%); international -2% to 118k (US tariffs, weak Europe and APAC; Brazil and LatAm strong). Capacity is not the limit: 1.5 mn annualised since late Jul-2026, a further module from Oct-2026, 2.0 mn at Cheyyar by Q2FY28. FY28E +10% (domestic +10% as the GST step-up laps; international +10% on Brazil CKD and a low base) and FY29E +8.8% (domestic +8.5%, international +12%). Brokers: FY27E 1.42-1.43 mn (PL, MOSL, ICICI Direct; monthly basis), FY28E 1.59-1.60 mn.

assumptions._revPerUnitWhy: Revenue per motorcycle = consolidated revenue / RE volume (FY26 Rs190,621; FY25 Rs188,158). Built in `build`: motorcycle realisation +2% a year (FY26 Rs162,440 = two-wheeler revenue Rs19,947 cr / volume; price rises of 0.85% in Jan-2026 and 1.75% on most 350cc models in Apr-2026, against a lower share of higher-priced international and >350cc bikes) plus allied revenue (spares, accessories, apparel, warranties, after-sales services, export incentives: Rs3,460 cr in FY26, +21.6%) growing +20% / +15% / +13%. Q1FY27 revenue per unit was Rs199,207 (+3.2% YoY) on a 15.3% international revenue share; H2 is domestic-heavy (festive), so the full year is lower.
assumptions._marginWhy: EBITDA margin (Screener basis, before other income and JV share): 26.2% FY24, 25.0% FY25, 24.7% FY26, 24.0% in Q1FY27 (gross margin 41.5%, -270bp YoY: a 4-4.5% commodity and process-cost hit, offset 1.2% by the April price rise, 0.4% value engineering and lower marketing). FY27E 24.2%: commodities 'softening' (management, Jul-2026) but marketing is being ramped up again in the 125th year, Flying Flea (EV) start-up costs and new stores. FY28E 24.8% and FY29E 25.0%: operating leverage at Cheyyar, value engineering on the J-platform, commodities normal. We do not return to FY24's 26.2%: management now prioritises volume over margin (MOSL), and >350cc mix (higher margin) has not recovered. Street: FY27E 24.3-24.6%, FY28E 25.2-25.5%.
assumptions._capexWhy: Cash capex Rs1,039 cr (FY25) and Rs1,275 cr (FY26). Committed: Cheyyar brownfield Rs958 cr (approved Feb-2026; 2.0 mn capacity by FY27-28), Tada (Andhra Pradesh) greenfield phase 1 Rs1,225 cr (approved 29-Jul-2026; +0.45 mn by FY2029-30, in modules), EV (Flying Flea L-platform), tooling for new models and maintenance. PL models Rs1,610 cr / Rs1,927 cr for FY27E / FY28E. The proposed Volvo Financial Services JV (up to Rs750 cr for 50%) is an investment, not capex, and is not in our treasury forecast (timing and approvals unknown).
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs840 cr = 11.6% of average gross block (Rs7,217 cr). Q1FY27 jumped to Rs278 cr (Rs1,110 cr annualised) as the Flying Flea line, the first Cheyyar module and tools and dies were capitalised (average gross block +Rs346 cr, CFO). The engine holds CWIP flat (Rs736 cr) and depreciates capex at once. 12.5% gives ~Rs1,070 cr in FY27E.

otherTreasury._why: Bank deposits Rs5,921 cr (more than 12 months Rs2,909 cr + less than 12 months Rs3,012 cr, other financial assets, AR FY26 consolidated note 11) and bill discounting for VECV's vendors Rs451 cr (note 10, earns 8.3-9.2%) sit in Screener's other assets / loans: they are treasury, not working capital.

assumptions._treasuryWhy: Engine workaround: Screener's 'investments' (Rs17,496 cr at Mar-26) include Rs3,723 cr carrying value of VECV (equity method) and Rs181 cr of strategic equity (Stark Future, Flamesun) that earn no interest, and the engine adds the whole VECV profit share to cash every year. The yield is set so that treasury income equals ~6.5% of the true average treasury (Mar-26: cash Rs256 cr + debt funds and bonds Rs13,591 cr + deposits Rs5,921 cr + bill discounting Rs451 cr - borrowings Rs514 cr = Rs19,705 cr). FY26 treasury income: interest Rs474 cr + fund gains Rs746 cr = Rs1,219 cr, 6.5% of average gross treasury. The build and reconciliation are in EICHERMOT.ctx.js.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Non-treasury other income = Eicher's 54.4% share of VECV profit (Rs838 / 967 / 1,084 cr, block `vecv`) + recurring items (facilitation income Rs69 cr, grants, write-backs, misc.: Rs100 / 110 / 120 cr). Exchange gains (Rs140 cr in FY26) are not forecast. FY26: other income Rs1,487 cr + VECV share Rs798 cr = Rs2,284 cr (Screener Rs2,225 cr after Rs57 cr exceptional items); TTM to Jun-26 Rs2,315 cr.
assumptions._interestLabel: Interest cost (leases, SIPCOT soft loan, working-capital lines)
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs72 cr; Q1FY27 Rs22 cr. Borrowings Rs514 cr at Mar-26 (incl. Rs195 cr leases).
assumptions._taxWhy: Tax on PBT including the VECV share, which is already after VECV's own tax: 25.5% on PBT excluding the JV share (FY26 24.9%, Q1FY27 26.3%) is ~22.7% of total PBT (FY26 22.3%). Checked each year in EICHERMOT.ctx.js.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Dividend per share Rs51 (FY24), Rs70 (FY25), Rs82 (FY26): 35%, 41% and 41% of consolidated EPS.

build._note: Royal Enfield revenue build (financial-statement volumes). Revenue = (domestic + international volume) x motorcycle realisation + allied revenue. FY26 actual: two-wheelers Rs19,947.29 cr, spares and components Rs1,541.26 cr, accessories and allied (traded) Rs1,368.70 cr, warranties Rs120.32 cr, other operating revenue Rs429.99 cr (AR FY26 consolidated note 28). Checked against model revenue in EICHERMOT.ctx.js.
build._why: Domestic: Apr-Aug +28%, Sep-Mar +12% against the GST-boosted base. International: -2% (P&L basis Q1 -2.4%; monthly exports Apr-Aug -9%), then recovery with CKD in Brazil and Indonesia. Realisation: list price rises ~1.5-2% a year less negative mix. Allied: Q1FY27 +23% (accessories and apparel +30%, service job cards +20%; accessories penetration 87%).

vecv._note: VE Commercial Vehicles (54.4% Eicher, 45.6% Volvo; joint control, equity-accounted). Consolidated VECV P&L from the Eicher investor presentation; EBITDA = revenue less operating costs (FY26 Rs2,501 cr; the company quotes Rs2,563 cr). FY26 PAT Rs1,466.6 cr after a Rs58.8 cr exceptional charge (Rs1,525 cr before). Eicher's share = 54.4% of PAT.
vecv._why: Volume: Q1FY27 24,815 (+14.8%; HD trucks +15.2%, LMD +16.1%, SCV Pro X 1,041, buses +2%); FY26 103,404 (+14.7% vs industry +13%) helped by the Sep-2025 GST cut on trucks and buses (28% to 18%), so H2FY27 faces a high base. FY27E +10% (PARIVARTAN NCR replacement scheme, SCV ramp-up), FY28-29E +6% (mid-cycle). Realisation +1.5% in FY27 (2% price rise in Apr-2026, diluted by small trucks), then +2.5%. EBITDA margin 8.2% in Q1FY27 (commodities), 9.2% in FY26 (our basis): 8.6% / 9.0% / 9.2%. Street FY27E PAT Rs1,475-1,528 cr (MOSL, PL); ICICI Direct FY28E Rs1,730 cr.

dcf._betaWhy: Net cash; discretionary but brand-led demand; below-market sensitivity (Ke 11.9%).
dcf._tgWhy: India's nominal GDP grows ~10%; premium motorcycles are under-penetrated and Royal Enfield has a global brand. House range 5-6%; 6%.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~11% to 8% over 15 years: volume 5-6% plus price and mix.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin held near 24.5%: scale and pricing power against rising competition and EV costs.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex falls from ~5% to 4% of revenue (capacity plus new platforms).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Premiumisation keeps compounding: domestic volumes grow ~3 points a year faster than our base (new 250-750cc launches, Hunter and Classic pulling in first-time buyers, Pay Commission cash), exports recover with Brazil and Indonesia CKD, and the >350cc mix returns; EBITDA margin ~26%, close to the FY24 peak; VECV grows with the replacement scheme.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: The GST boost proves a one-off pull-forward: from H2FY27 domestic growth falls to low single digits against the high base, competition in 350-450cc (Honda, Triumph, Jawa-Yezdi, Harley-Hero) takes share, exports stay weak and commodity inflation persists; EBITDA margin ~23%, back to FY22-FY23 levels; a CV downturn hits VECV.

sotp._note: Written by tools/authoring/EICHERMOT.sotp.js from EICHERMOT.ctx.js (derived multiples, rounded to the nearest half-turn).

methods.name: SOTP (RE P/E + VECV P/E)
methods.why: How the street values Eicher: a sum of the parts, Royal Enfield on P/E and VECV on P/E or EV/EBITDA. Royal Enfield: its own one-year-forward P/E median since Apr-2021 with VECV stripped out, cut by the auto-OEM sector de-rating; VECV: Ashok Leyland's forward P/E median (the closest listed CV maker) cut by the same de-rating. The engine has no P/E-based SOTP, so the SOTP value is carried as an implied multiple of consolidated Sep-28E EPS (written by tools/authoring/EICHERMOT.sotp.js).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Counts net cash at face value; VECV only at its carrying value inside net cash.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether Royal Enfield's cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF, Ke 11.9%, terminal growth 6%, plus net cash (VECV only at carrying value).

cover.headline: India's best two-wheeler franchise, priced for more than its own history allows
cover.lead: Royal Enfield sells ~85% of India's mid-size (250-750cc) motorcycles and earns a 24-25% EBITDA margin, far above any mass-market rival. GST 2.0 (Sep-2025) cut the tax on its 350cc range, ~92% of domestic volume, from 28% to 18%; volumes rose 22% in FY26 to 12.3 lakh and 27% in Q1FY27, and capacity is going from 1.5 mn to 2.45 mn by FY30. Eicher also owns 54.4% of VECV, India's #1 light-and-medium truck maker, which it equity-accounts. The street values the stock on a **sum of the parts: Royal Enfield on 29-35x FY28E P/E plus VECV**. We forecast EPS of ₹221.0 / ₹254.0 / ₹285.0 for FY27-29E, close to the street. Applying the house rule to each part (**Royal Enfield 23.5x Sep-28E EPS of ₹232.1, VECV 16.5x Eicher's share of ₹37.4**) gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}})**: **we initiate with SELL.** Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹6,166, DCF ₹6,054. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: Demand is strong, broad and not capacity-bound any more
arguments.p: Q1FY27 domestic volumes rose 32% (the four 350s +34%), then +34% in July and +11% in August; enquiries and bookings grow faster than dispatches and dealer stock is only 10-12 days. A new Cheyyar module took capacity to 1.5 mn in July; the next comes in October. International revenue crossed ₹1,000 cr in a quarter for the first time.

arguments.h: But FY27 is a year of two halves
arguments.p: From Sep-2026 Royal Enfield laps the GST-boosted base (Q3FY26: 3 lakh domestic, +26% festive). The >350cc range only got back to pre-GST volumes in July after its tax rose to 40%, and exports fell 9% in Apr-Aug. We model domestic +12% for Sep-Mar, i.e. {{F.volume.0|num}} motorcycles in FY27E (+{{as.volume.growth.0|n1}}%), then ~10% and ~9% growth.

arguments.h: Margins: 24-25%, not the 26-31% of the past
arguments.p: EBITDA margin was 31% in FY18, 26.2% in FY24, 24.7% in FY26 and 24.0% in Q1FY27 (a 4-4.5% commodity hit). Management now chases volume (refreshes at little extra price, more advertising), the EV brand is a start-up cost and depreciation jumped 40% in Q1. We model {{F.ebitdaMargin.0|pct}} / {{F.ebitdaMargin.1|pct}} / {{F.ebitdaMargin.2|pct}} and EPS growth of ~12% a year for FY26-29E, against 33% in FY21-26.

arguments.h: Valuation: the premium is not in the history
arguments.p: At ₹7,150 the stock trades at 28.1x our FY28E EPS. Its one-year-forward P/E has a median of 24.0x since Apr-2021 (25.1x for Royal Enfield with VECV stripped out); auto peers were 6.9% below their five-year medians on 30-Sep-2026. That gives 23.5x for Royal Enfield, against the street's 29-35x. At the street's median 30x our target would be ~₹7,580: the whole gap is the multiple, not the earnings.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): festive-season dispatches, the margin after the commodity peak, and the cost of the Flying Flea roll-out.
Festive retail (Oct-Nov 2026) against the GST-boosted base of Oct-Nov 2025: the first real test of whether the GST step-up in demand is permanent.
Capacity: the second Cheyyar module (early Oct-2026) and 2 mn units by FY27-28; whether dealer stock can be rebuilt above 10-12 days.
Launches: Flying Flea S6 and city expansion, 650cc refreshes (Bullet 650, Classic 650 anniversary edition), Indonesia CKD decision.
VECV: the PARIVARTAN replacement scheme for Delhi-NCR, the CV cycle after the GST cut, and approval of the Volvo finance JV (up to ₹750 cr).

sections.title: Two businesses: Royal Enfield (all of the revenue) and 54.4% of VECV (a sixth of the profit)

blocks.p: Eicher Motors owns **Royal Enfield**, the world's oldest motorcycle brand in continuous production (1901) and the leader in mid-size motorcycles (250-750cc). It makes three engine platforms: the 350cc "J" single (Classic, Bullet, Hunter, Meteor, Goan Classic; ~92% of domestic volume), the 450cc "Sherpa" (Himalayan, Guerrilla) plus the 440cc Scram, and the 650cc twin (Interceptor, Continental GT, Super Meteor, Shotgun, Bear, Classic and Bullet 650). Since Apr-2026 it also sells an electric city motorcycle under a new brand, **Flying Flea**. Bikes are made in Chennai (Oragadam, Vallam Vadagal) and Cheyyar, and assembled from kits (CKD) in Thailand, Brazil, Argentina, Colombia, Nepal and Bangladesh. Revenue also includes spares, accessories, riding gear and service: "allied" business, ~15% of revenue.

Eicher also owns **54.4% of VE Commercial Vehicles (VECV)**, a joint venture with Sweden's Volvo (45.6%) formed in 2008. VECV makes Eicher trucks and buses, distributes Volvo trucks and buses in India and makes engines (VE Powertrain). Control is shared 50:50 by agreement, so VECV is not consolidated: Eicher books 54.4% of its profit as one line ("share of profit of joint venture"). **Eicher's reported revenue and EBITDA are therefore Royal Enfield alone.** Screener adds the VECV share to other income.

sections.title: From a near-dead brand in 2000 to a 12-lakh-a-year exporter; few acquisitions, one written-off JV

blocks.p: Eicher bought Enfield India in 1994. In the 2000s, under Siddhartha Lal, the group sold its tractor and other businesses, folded its own trucks into the Volvo JV (2008) and bet on Royal Enfield, whose Classic 350 took off after the Oragadam plant opened (2013). Volumes reached 8.3 lakh in FY19, fell to ~6 lakh in FY21-22 (new safety and insurance rules raised prices; Covid; chip shortages), and doubled again to 12.3 lakh by FY26 on the new J-platform 350s and GST 2.0.

sections.title: Premium motorcycles are the only growing part of the motorcycle market; GST 2.0 made the 350s cheaper

blocks.p: India sold 2.2 crore two-wheelers in FY26 (+10.7%, a record above FY19), but motorcycles grew only 6.6% (scooters +18.5%). Within motorcycles, the mid-size segment is where the growth is: ~70,000 a month three years ago, ~120k a month now, after 20+ launches by rivals. Royal Enfield went from ~61k to ~101k a month (management, Jul-2026). It holds ~85% of the segment but only 9.1% of all Indian motorcycles: the headroom is in upgrading commuters, a quarter of RE buyers are first-time buyers.

bullets: **Rare earths (2025).** China's export curbs on rare-earth magnets disrupted Himalayan, Scram and Guerrilla 450 production in Q1FY26; output stabilised with alternative materials; Bajaj delayed an entry-level Chetak EV. Flying Flea launched Apr-2026, roughly the timing planned in 2025 ('towards the end of FY26').

**Electric.** Flying Flea C6 launched on 9-Apr-2026 at Rs2.79 lakh (Rs1.99 lakh with battery-as-a-service), ex-showroom; deliveries from 19-Jun-2026; 100+ by end-Jul-2026; plan: one Bengaluru store, then 10 touchpoints, then ~6 cities one by one; S6 scrambler next. Premium electric motorcycles are a tiny market in India today; the EV threat to Royal Enfield is long-dated, but its answer is still a one-city experiment.

**Commodities and supply (2026).** 2026 input inflation (aluminium, steel, copper, precious metals, crude) after the West Asia conflict; LPG shortages and election-related labour shortages in Apr-May 2026; RE's net hit 4-4.5% of cost in Q1FY27, 'softening' by late July.

**Abroad.** The global middleweight market is ~0.8-1.0 mn a year; Royal Enfield has 8-9%. Brazil is now its biggest export market; the US (tariffs), Europe ("market adjustment") and Thailand are weak; Indonesia caps imports at ~10,000 a year.

**Commercial vehicles.** The CV industry grew ~13% in FY26 (VECV 14.7%), helped by the GST cut on trucks and buses and infrastructure spending; the Delhi-NCR PARIVARTAN scheme targets 2.07 lakh old trucks and buses.

sections.title: Rivals are many but small: RE still had ~82% of 350-450cc dispatches in June 2026

blocks.p: Every large two-wheeler maker has now entered Royal Enfield's segment, mostly through foreign brands: Bajaj with Triumph (Speed 400, Scrambler 400, and from 2026 a 350) and KTM; Hero with Harley-Davidson (X440) and its own Mavrick; Honda with the CB350 and H'ness; Mahindra-backed Classic Legends with Jawa, Yezdi and BSA; TVS with BMW (310s) and Norton. None has come close: in June 2026 Royal Enfield's 350s alone outsold all rivals in 350-450cc by ~4 to 1. The risks are slower share erosion at the edges (Honda CB350 +62% YoY) and price pressure if a rival with scale (Bajaj-Triumph, Honda) decides to buy share.

sections.title: Royal Enfield: volume-led growth, a cheaper mix, and margins a notch lower

blocks.p: Royal Enfield sold 12,27,977 motorcycles in FY26 (+22.4%): 11,07,343 in India (+23%) and 1,20,634 abroad (+20%). Q1FY27 was its best quarter ever at 3,32,940 (+27%; India 301,174, abroad 31,766). Momentum held into the festive build-up: +34% in July and +11% in August against a stronger base (Apr-Aug 5,75,138, +23%; domestic +28%, exports −9%). The 350s carry the growth: ~93% of Q1FY27 domestic volume (280,136 of 301,174). Above 350cc, the Guerrilla 450 (~2,500 a month) and the 650 twins (~4,000-4,200) only got back to their pre-GST run-rate in July; the Himalayan, Super Meteor and Shotgun were still weak.

Revenue per motorcycle tells the mix story. Two-wheeler revenue per unit rose only 1.7% in FY26 to ₹1,62,440, despite price rises, because the cheaper 350s grew fastest. Total revenue per unit (incl. allied) was ₹190,621; Q1FY27's ₹199,207 (+3.2% YoY) was helped by price (+1.2% QoQ), a higher international share (15.3% of revenue) and allied growth (+23%). Allied revenue (spares, accessories, apparel, service) was ₹3,460 cr in FY26 (+22%): steady, recurring, and in our view higher-margin than motorcycles (the company does not disclose its margin).

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** Royal Enfield has one of the few genuine moats in Indian manufacturing: a brand that defines its category, a cost position from running one engine platform at ~1 mn units a year, and a community and service network rivals have not copied in a decade of trying. But the moat is narrower than the market share suggests. It is strongest in 350cc commuter-upgrade bikes, where price matters; above 350cc the GST rise showed buyers are price-sensitive; and in electric motorcycles RE starts from zero. The moat protects **volume and share**, not an ever-rising margin.

sections.title: Revenue up 2.7x and EPS 4x since FY21, but margins peaked in FY24

blocks.p: Eicher's consolidated revenue (Royal Enfield only) went from ₹8,720 cr in FY21, a Covid year, to ₹23,408 cr in FY26: about 22% a year. EPS went from ₹49.3 to ₹201.1, about 33% a year, helped by three things on top of volume: operating leverage, a growing share of VECV's profit (₹0 in FY21, ₹798 cr in FY26) and rising treasury income (₹482 cr to ₹1,487 cr). Before that, FY19-FY21 were poor years: volumes fell from 8.3 lakh to 6.1 lakh as Royal Enfield raised prices for new safety rules and Covid hit, and EBITDA margin slid from 30% to 20%.

sections.title: High returns on a small asset base; capex now doubling for capacity and EVs

blocks.p: Royal Enfield needs little capital. Net fixed assets were ₹3,852 cr at Mar-2026 against ₹23,408 cr of revenue, and working capital is negative in most years because dealers pay before suppliers are paid. Cash from operations over FY21-26 was ₹18,550 cr, capex ₹4,988 cr and dividends ₹5,369 cr; the rest built a treasury of ~₹19,700 cr (net of debt, excluding VECV). Reported ROE was 24% in FY24-FY26, held down by that cash; on operating capital alone returns are well above 50%. Capex is now rising: Cheyyar brownfield (₹958 cr, 2 mn capacity by FY27-28), the Tada greenfield (₹1,225 cr phase 1, +0.45 mn by FY2029-30), the Flying Flea EV platform and new models.

Even so, the treasury keeps growing by ₹3,000-4,000 cr a year. sections.title: Earnings quality: clean accounts and strong cash, but a third of profit is not from motorcycles

bullets: **Cash backs profit once you strip out non-cash items.** Reported operating cash flow was 87% of net profit in FY26 and 84% in FY25, because profit includes the VECV share (₹798 cr in FY26, of which only ₹218 cr came in as dividends) and treasury income (shown under investing). Against Royal Enfield's own after-tax profit (~₹3,742 cr), cash from operations of ₹4,805 cr is ~128%.

**Treasury income is large and partly mark-to-market.** FY26 other income of ₹1,487 cr included ₹746 cr of gains on debt mutual funds, ₹474 cr of interest and ₹140 cr of exchange gains. Fund gains rise when bond yields fall; a rate reversal would cut them. We forecast treasury income at ~6.5% of the true treasury (FY27E ₹1,369 cr).

**VECV is equity-accounted.** Eicher owns 54.4% but shares control with Volvo, so VECV's ₹27,077 cr of revenue and its debt-free balance sheet stay off Eicher's books; only the profit share appears. That is the correct accounting, but it makes Eicher's P/E a blend of a motorcycle company and a truck company.

**Some losses bypass EPS.** The ₹302 cr fall in the value of the Stark Future stake (FY25) went through OCI; the Eicher Polaris JV loss (₹238 cr in FY18-19) was booked as exceptional. FY26 had a ₹55 cr exceptional charge for the new Labour Codes.

**Related-party lending.** Eicher discounts bills for VECV's suppliers (₹451 cr at Mar-26, at 8.3-9.2%): a sensible use of cash, but a credit exposure to the JV's supply chain that sits inside "treasury".

**Disclosure.** One reportable segment; model-wise volumes are not disclosed (only 350cc vs above in monthly releases); the domestic/international split of motorcycle revenue is not given. Volumes in the financial statements differ from the monthly releases (CKD counting).

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: GREEN.** Unqualified audit by S.R. Batliboi & Co., simple balance sheet, no debt, negative working capital and no aggressive capitalisation visible. The watch items are the size of mark-to-market treasury gains and the VECV-related bill discounting.

Separately it carries its 54.4% of VECV at ₹3,723 cr (cost ₹5 cr plus retained profits) and strategic equity stakes at ₹181 cr. Screener's "investments" line (₹17,496 cr) mixes the treasury funds with the VECV stake. Inventory is ~55 days of revenue; receivables only ~6 days; suppliers are paid in ~76 days.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Eicher Motors (consolidated, Rs crore). Consolidated revenue and EBITDA are Royal Enfield only (motorcycles, spares, accessories, apparel, services; India plus the international subsidiaries). VE Commercial Vehicles (VECV, Eicher 54.4%, joint control with Volvo) is a joint venture accounted for by the equity method: none of its revenue or EBITDA is consolidated and Eicher books 54.4% of VECV's profit as one line ('share of profit of joint venture'), which Screener adds to other income. So the model is: RE volume x revenue per motorcycle (engine volume path; the domestic / international / allied build is in `build` and is checked against model revenue in tools/authoring/EICHERMOT.ctx.js) and VECV volume x realisation -> EBITDA -> PAT -> 54.4% share (block `vecv`), which enters `otherIncome`. Volumes are on the company's financial-statement basis (FY26 1,227,977 = domestic 1,107,343 + international 120,634), which differs slightly from the monthly sales releases (FY26 1,238,659) because CKD exports are counted differently. Screener's Net Profit equals Profit for EPS (no minorities), so no patchRaw. Valued on a sum of the parts (RE P/E + VECV P/E) as the street does; the engine carries the SOTP as an implied P/E on consolidated Sep-28E EPS (tools/authoring/EICHERMOT.sotp.js writes it).

volume._why: Royal Enfield motorcycles, financial-statement basis (FY26 1,227,977, +22.4%). FY27E +15.8% to 1.422 mn: Q1FY27 332,940 (+27.4%; domestic 301,174 +32%, international 31,766 -2%); monthly releases show Jul +34% and Aug +11% (Apr-Aug 575,138, +23%; domestic +28%, exports -9%). We assume domestic +12% for Sep-Mar against the GST-boosted base of FY26 (domestic Sep-Mar FY26 ~699k) -> domestic FY27E 1.304 mn (+17.8%); international -2% to 118k (US tariffs, weak Europe and APAC; Brazil and LatAm strong). Capacity is not the limit: 1.5 mn annualised since late Jul-2026, a further module from Oct-2026, 2.0 mn at Cheyyar by Q2FY28. FY28E +10% (domestic +10% as the GST step-up laps; international +10% on Brazil CKD and a low base) and FY29E +8.8% (domestic +8.5%, international +12%). Brokers: FY27E 1.42-1.43 mn (PL, MOSL, ICICI Direct; monthly basis), FY28E 1.59-1.60 mn.

assumptions._revPerUnitWhy: Revenue per motorcycle = consolidated revenue / RE volume (FY26 Rs190,621; FY25 Rs188,158). Built in `build`: motorcycle realisation +2% a year (FY26 Rs162,440 = two-wheeler revenue Rs19,947 cr / volume; price rises of 0.85% in Jan-2026 and 1.75% on most 350cc models in Apr-2026, against a lower share of higher-priced international and >350cc bikes) plus allied revenue (spares, accessories, apparel, warranties, after-sales services, export incentives: Rs3,460 cr in FY26, +21.6%) growing +20% / +15% / +13%. Q1FY27 revenue per unit was Rs199,207 (+3.2% YoY) on a 15.3% international revenue share; H2 is domestic-heavy (festive), so the full year is lower.
assumptions._marginWhy: EBITDA margin (Screener basis, before other income and JV share): 26.2% FY24, 25.0% FY25, 24.7% FY26, 24.0% in Q1FY27 (gross margin 41.5%, -270bp YoY: a 4-4.5% commodity and process-cost hit, offset 1.2% by the April price rise, 0.4% value engineering and lower marketing). FY27E 24.2%: commodities 'softening' (management, Jul-2026) but marketing is being ramped up again in the 125th year, Flying Flea (EV) start-up costs and new stores. FY28E 24.8% and FY29E 25.0%: operating leverage at Cheyyar, value engineering on the J-platform, commodities normal. We do not return to FY24's 26.2%: management now prioritises volume over margin (MOSL), and >350cc mix (higher margin) has not recovered. Street: FY27E 24.3-24.6%, FY28E 25.2-25.5%.
assumptions._capexWhy: Cash capex Rs1,039 cr (FY25) and Rs1,275 cr (FY26). Committed: Cheyyar brownfield Rs958 cr (approved Feb-2026; 2.0 mn capacity by FY27-28), Tada (Andhra Pradesh) greenfield phase 1 Rs1,225 cr (approved 29-Jul-2026; +0.45 mn by FY2029-30, in modules), EV (Flying Flea L-platform), tooling for new models and maintenance. PL models Rs1,610 cr / Rs1,927 cr for FY27E / FY28E. The proposed Volvo Financial Services JV (up to Rs750 cr for 50%) is an investment, not capex, and is not in our treasury forecast (timing and approvals unknown).
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs840 cr = 11.6% of average gross block (Rs7,217 cr). Q1FY27 jumped to Rs278 cr (Rs1,110 cr annualised) as the Flying Flea line, the first Cheyyar module and tools and dies were capitalised (average gross block +Rs346 cr, CFO). The engine holds CWIP flat (Rs736 cr) and depreciates capex at once. 12.5% gives ~Rs1,070 cr in FY27E.

otherTreasury._why: Bank deposits Rs5,921 cr (more than 12 months Rs2,909 cr + less than 12 months Rs3,012 cr, other financial assets, AR FY26 consolidated note 11) and bill discounting for VECV's vendors Rs451 cr (note 10, earns 8.3-9.2%) sit in Screener's other assets / loans: they are treasury, not working capital.

assumptions._treasuryWhy: Engine workaround: Screener's 'investments' (Rs17,496 cr at Mar-26) include Rs3,723 cr carrying value of VECV (equity method) and Rs181 cr of strategic equity (Stark Future, Flamesun) that earn no interest, and the engine adds the whole VECV profit share to cash every year. The yield is set so that treasury income equals ~6.5% of the true average treasury (Mar-26: cash Rs256 cr + debt funds and bonds Rs13,591 cr + deposits Rs5,921 cr + bill discounting Rs451 cr - borrowings Rs514 cr = Rs19,705 cr). FY26 treasury income: interest Rs474 cr + fund gains Rs746 cr = Rs1,219 cr, 6.5% of average gross treasury. The build and reconciliation are in EICHERMOT.ctx.js.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Non-treasury other income = Eicher's 54.4% share of VECV profit (Rs838 / 967 / 1,084 cr, block `vecv`) + recurring items (facilitation income Rs69 cr, grants, write-backs, misc.: Rs100 / 110 / 120 cr). Exchange gains (Rs140 cr in FY26) are not forecast. FY26: other income Rs1,487 cr + VECV share Rs798 cr = Rs2,284 cr (Screener Rs2,225 cr after Rs57 cr exceptional items); TTM to Jun-26 Rs2,315 cr.
assumptions._interestLabel: Interest cost (leases, SIPCOT soft loan, working-capital lines)
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs72 cr; Q1FY27 Rs22 cr. Borrowings Rs514 cr at Mar-26 (incl. Rs195 cr leases).
assumptions._taxWhy: Tax on PBT including the VECV share, which is already after VECV's own tax: 25.5% on PBT excluding the JV share (FY26 24.9%, Q1FY27 26.3%) is ~22.7% of total PBT (FY26 22.3%). Checked each year in EICHERMOT.ctx.js.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Dividend per share Rs51 (FY24), Rs70 (FY25), Rs82 (FY26): 35%, 41% and 41% of consolidated EPS.

build._note: Royal Enfield revenue build (financial-statement volumes). Revenue = (domestic + international volume) x motorcycle realisation + allied revenue. FY26 actual: two-wheelers Rs19,947.29 cr, spares and components Rs1,541.26 cr, accessories and allied (traded) Rs1,368.70 cr, warranties Rs120.32 cr, other operating revenue Rs429.99 cr (AR FY26 consolidated note 28). Checked against model revenue in EICHERMOT.ctx.js.
build._why: Domestic: Apr-Aug +28%, Sep-Mar +12% against the GST-boosted base. International: -2% (P&L basis Q1 -2.4%; monthly exports Apr-Aug -9%), then recovery with CKD in Brazil and Indonesia. Realisation: list price rises ~1.5-2% a year less negative mix. Allied: Q1FY27 +23% (accessories and apparel +30%, service job cards +20%; accessories penetration 87%).

vecv._note: VE Commercial Vehicles (54.4% Eicher, 45.6% Volvo; joint control, equity-accounted). Consolidated VECV P&L from the Eicher investor presentation; EBITDA = revenue less operating costs (FY26 Rs2,501 cr; the company quotes Rs2,563 cr). FY26 PAT Rs1,466.6 cr after a Rs58.8 cr exceptional charge (Rs1,525 cr before). Eicher's share = 54.4% of PAT.
vecv._why: Volume: Q1FY27 24,815 (+14.8%; HD trucks +15.2%, LMD +16.1%, SCV Pro X 1,041, buses +2%); FY26 103,404 (+14.7% vs industry +13%) helped by the Sep-2025 GST cut on trucks and buses (28% to 18%), so H2FY27 faces a high base. FY27E +10% (PARIVARTAN NCR replacement scheme, SCV ramp-up), FY28-29E +6% (mid-cycle). Realisation +1.5% in FY27 (2% price rise in Apr-2026, diluted by small trucks), then +2.5%. EBITDA margin 8.2% in Q1FY27 (commodities), 9.2% in FY26 (our basis): 8.6% / 9.0% / 9.2%. Street FY27E PAT Rs1,475-1,528 cr (MOSL, PL); ICICI Direct FY28E Rs1,730 cr.

dcf._betaWhy: Net cash; discretionary but brand-led demand; below-market sensitivity (Ke 11.9%).
dcf._tgWhy: India's nominal GDP grows ~10%; premium motorcycles are under-penetrated and Royal Enfield has a global brand. House range 5-6%; 6%.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~11% to 8% over 15 years: volume 5-6% plus price and mix.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin held near 24.5%: scale and pricing power against rising competition and EV costs.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex falls from ~5% to 4% of revenue (capacity plus new platforms).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Premiumisation keeps compounding: domestic volumes grow ~3 points a year faster than our base (new 250-750cc launches, Hunter and Classic pulling in first-time buyers, Pay Commission cash), exports recover with Brazil and Indonesia CKD, and the >350cc mix returns; EBITDA margin ~26%, close to the FY24 peak; VECV grows with the replacement scheme.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: The GST boost proves a one-off pull-forward: from H2FY27 domestic growth falls to low single digits against the high base, competition in 350-450cc (Honda, Triumph, Jawa-Yezdi, Harley-Hero) takes share, exports stay weak and commodity inflation persists; EBITDA margin ~23%, back to FY22-FY23 levels; a CV downturn hits VECV.
